annotations.text:
A — THE HOUSE

Symmetrical, centred, bone and cognac. The grammar every established maison shares: thin rules, a Didone wordmark, the product in a generous frame.

Strength: reads expensive instantly. Nobody has to be taught how to look at it.

Tradeoff: it is the most borrowed language in luxury. Safe, and therefore the least memorable of the three.

B — THE BENCH   (my recommendation)

Maison polish plus a specification layer: brass leader lines pointing at real construction, mono lot numbers, the vocabulary of a workshop.

Strength: it is the only one that could belong to Carson and no one else. The annotations point AT the shoe, so the type sells the product instead of competing with it — the 'product, not art project' test.

Tradeoff: the technical layer must stay disciplined. Overdo it and it turns into a diagram.

C — THE EDIT

Fashion editorial. Sand and oxblood, one heavy grotesk, the shoe rotated and breaking across the panel edge.

Strength: the most contemporary and by far the most Instagram-native — this crops into a grid without any work.

Tradeoff: it reads fashion-season rather than permanent, and heavy grotesk at this scale is currently everywhere. It will date faster than A or B.

Revised against the company profile.

Every claim on screen is now documented: est. 1995, Italian design association, own tanneries in Kolkata and Chennai, SA-8000 certified, made in Agra. 'Twenty-five years' was wrong — it is thirty.

No client is named. The three credentials above are stronger than the client list and carry no legal risk.

Goodyear welt and vegetable-tanning stay absent until you confirm them. Prices show as [YOUR PRICE].

All three use the same drawn shoe so you are judging art direction, not photography.
